title: Investment Fraud and Online Scam Platforms
summary: How fake investment platforms, crypto-asset scams and boiler rooms operate, how they move victim funds, and how investigators identify the people and infrastructure behind them.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How fake investment platforms, crypto-asset scams and boiler rooms operate, how they move victim funds, and how investigators identify the people and infrastructure behind them.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the features of investment fraud and fake trading platforms
Trace victim funds through payment and crypto-asset channels
Identify the infrastructure and actors behind scam operations
Syllabus: Boiler rooms, clone firms and fake trading platforms
Payment routes, intermediary accounts and off-ramps
Websites, domains, advertising and scam infrastructure
Intended Audience: Fraud, economic crime and cybercrime investigators
FIU analysts handling fraud-related reports and urgent requests
Victim liaison, prevention and disruption officers working with the financial sector
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, cybercrime or financial crime investigation is helpful. No technical background in cyber security or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2023), Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-Enabled Fraud
FATF (2022), Partnering in the Fight Against Financial Crime: Data Protection, Technology and Private Sector Information Sharing
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
